Classic Solomon Analysis (Teaching Flow)

Source: vignettes/classic-solomon.Rmd
classic-solomon.Rmd

This vignette demonstrates the textbook route: 2×2 posttest ANOVA on the four cells, then ANCOVA on the pretested cells and a posttest-only t-test, with an optional Stouffer Z combination (Braver & Braver, 1988), plus cautions from later exchanges.

References: Huck & Sandler (1973); Braver & Braver (1988); Sawilowsky & Markman (1988, 1990) and replies.

library(solomonR); set.seed(123)
n <- 40
y_pre <- c(rnorm(n), rnorm(n), rep(NA, 2*n))
treat <- c(rep(1,n), rep(0,n), rep(1,n), rep(0,n))
prein <- c(rep(1,2*n), rep(0,2*n))
y_post <- rnorm(4*n) + 0.5*treat # no sensitization
res <- fit_solomon_classic(y_post, treat, prein, y_pre, combine_with_stouffer = TRUE)
res$aov
## # A tibble: 4 × 6
##   term               df   sumsq meansq statistic   p.value
##   <chr>           <dbl>   <dbl>  <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>
## 1 treat               1  12.5   12.5      13.7    0.000293
## 2 pretested           1   0.157  0.157     0.172  0.679   
## 3 treat:pretested     1   0.116  0.116     0.127  0.722   
## 4 Residuals         156 143.     0.914    NA     NA
res$ancova
## # A tibble: 3 × 5
##   term           estimate std.error statistic p.value
##   <chr>             <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1 (Intercept)      -0.105     0.150    -0.699 0.487  
## 2 treat[idx_pre]    0.607     0.213     2.86  0.00551
## 3 y_pre[idx_pre]    0.123     0.116     1.06  0.291
res$t_unpretested
## # A tibble: 1 × 10
##   estimate estimate1 estimate2 statistic p.value parameter conf.low conf.high
##      <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>     <dbl>   <dbl>     <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>
## 1   -0.506    0.0106     0.517     -2.36  0.0210      77.6   -0.934   -0.0785
## # ℹ 2 more variables: method <chr>, alternative <chr>
res$stouffer
